subject: System Design
title: Team Size and Architecture
description: A short lesson to help you apply Team Size and Architecture.

hook.text: Conway's Law: organizations design systems that mirror their communication structure. Architecture follows teams.

buildup.text: A 5-person team doesn't need microservices. The communication overhead exceeds the modularity benefits.

discovery.text: Amazon's two-pizza rule: each service should be owned by a team small enough to be fed by two pizzas.

twist.text: Splitting services without splitting teams creates shared ownership. No one feels responsible; quality drops.

climax.text: Architecture should match team structure. Split services when you split teams, not before.

punchline.text: Architecture mirrors teams — split services when you split teams.

quiz.question: What does Conway's Law state?
options: Organizations design systems that mirror their communication structure
